thread:
Mia: Quick heads-up — Valora onboarding. They've been reporting 250–400ms tail latency on long chat turns and we've got a renewal check in ~6w. Want to propose a proactive perf plan (quant + model swap + routing) before it becomes a risk. Thoughts?

Neal: Saw the traces. Long-turn tails come from KV cache misses + the 7B fp16 model. My suggestion: canary q4_0 quantized variant + fallback to the fp16 only on hallucination/quality regression. Also prefix-KV caching for the 90th pct tokens.

Jordan: Can we route these customers to a lower-cost region to reduce p95? Valora is in EU so we can try eu-west-low-latency pool. Need to check Dedicated pool capacity for the canary capacity.

Alice: From AE side — if we can show a 20% cost drop and p95 < 200ms in a week, renewal convo is much easier. Need comms plan for the customer and a short demo.

OpsBot: alert: valora-prod model=rw-infer-7b latency_p95=398ms errors=0.4% span=last_24h

Neal: Plan details: 1) Build q4_0 artifact of rw-infer-7b (no extra pruning). 2) Run A/B canary: 5% traffic to q4, 95% to fp16 for 48h. 3) Evaluate on Valora eval set (prompt slices + ground truth) for perplexity/ROUGE ~ compare. 4) If <2% quality regression, promote and enable prefix caching + routing policy that prefers q4 for high-concurrency requests.

Mia: Thanks. Can we add a fallback routing policy: if response_confidence < threshold OR latency spikes, route to fp16? Also want to capture customer's feedback post-demo.

Neal: Yep — implement function-level routing: if model_confidence_score < 0.85 OR generation_length>1024 -> route fp16. I'll add a canary eval script. Example eval command:```bash
python infra/eval/canary_eval.py --model rw-infer-7b-q4 --dataset valora_eval.json --metrics rouge,bleu,latency
```

Jordan: I'll reserve 2x smaller GPUs in eu-west for the canary and add autoscale policy: min=1, max=3 for the q4 nodes. Also enable trace sampling = 10% to get detailed token-level latencies.

Alice: I'll prep a 15-min demo + a 1-pager with the expected cost delta and quality notes. Can someone drop the expected cost delta numbers here?

Neal: Rough math: q4 gives ~2.4x speedup on T4-style instances and ~40% lower token cost given our batching assumptions. So expect 30–45% unit cost reduction depending on workload. Will include exact numbers after a fast bench.

Mia: Action items — Neal: bench + push q4 artifact + run canary (owner). Jordan: provision canary region capacity + enable traces (owner). Alice: customer demo + 1-pager (owner). I'll schedule an enablement call and capture Valora's feedback form after demo. Ping me when canary metrics are live. :thumbsup:

Alice: :thumbsup: scheduling demo for next Tue 10am CET. Mia can you own the invite?

Neal: Starting bench now, will post a short log snippet when ready.

Jordan: Provisioned canary nodes — cluster eu-west-qcanary up.

Mia: Great — keep updates in this thread. If we hit >2% quality drop we abort and collect logs for SRE/MLE postmortem.

OpsBot: canary_job_started job_id=canary-309876-1 model=rw-infer-7b-q4 time=3098765450

Neal: Bench done — p95(q4)=180ms, p95(fp16)=420ms on same test set. Rough quality delta: rouge_drop=0.9%. Uploading eval artifacts to /tmp/valora_canary_results.json and will attach shortly.

Mia: This looks promising. Will draft the renewal talking points and customer-facing note. Thanks team. ✅
